data.narrative:
Cellares is a Series C-stage biotech company that has raised $350M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 private companies at the same stage and sector (Biotech & Health), alongside 3 public comparables, though public-company methods face data constraints.

Two valuation methods triangulate a range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $12M total-raised proxy, implying $20M. Peer-median anchoring across three same-stage biotech firms—Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B)—yields a median of $3.8B and a range of $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring using a 8.1x price-to-sales multiple across three public biotech tickers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) cannot be applied, as target revenue is not disclosed. 

Synthesizing the two applicable methods produces a triangulated range of $17M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $1.9B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Cellares' technology de-risking and commercial trajectory relative to peers. Stage-progression yields materially lower results than peer-median analysis, suggesting either that the $12M raised proxy understates true capital deployment or that peer valuations embed substantial upside expectations. Revenue disclosure would tighten the valuation envelope considerably.
